feedback:
Written before this candidate has raced, so no outcome is stated for it. The candidate is the iteration-6 design (score 696.6, best so far) with one geometry change: the seven sensors move forward from y 0.06 to y 0.07 m. The controller is the iteration-6 set (kp 4.8, kd 0.9, ki 0.5, base_speed 1.3, last_direction, same weights), and the sensor footprint (12 mm) and lateral span (±3 cm, 1 cm spacing) are unchanged. The y value is inside the allowed range (max 0.08).

The evidence supports a single, isolated test. Iteration 6 finished 20/20 on oval and 20/20 on s-bend, but slalom finished 0/20 with progress 0.47 and 1.25 line-loss events per run. Iteration 7 showed that raising kp to 5.0 and kd to 1.0 gave little slalom gain (progress 0.53) and cost s-bend finishes (17/20), so the controller is near its useful limit. Iteration 8 showed that widening the array to 16 mm at ±4 cm hurt s-bend (14/20) and slalom progress (0.37), so the sensing layout should stay at iteration 6. That leaves look-ahead as the untested lever. Iteration 6 is the only raced design at y 0.06, and the iteration-3 move from y 0.05 to 0.06 came with improved oval and s-bend results, although that change was confounded with controller changes.

Caution: moving the sensors further ahead adds sensing lag at low speed and could raise max_error on s-bend. Oval has a large margin (steering_oscillation 0.232, max_error 0.0095), so an oval regression would be a signal of the forward shift, not of the gains.

How to read the next race: if s-bend finishes hold at 18/20 or better and slalom progress rises above 0.47 with line_loss_events falling, keep y 0.07 and consider y 0.08 (the allowed maximum) as the next single step. If s-bend finishes fall below 18/20 or s-bend max_error rises above about 0.02, the forward shift is hurting, so return y to 0.06 and treat iteration 6 as the baseline. If slalom progress is flat near 0.47 with line_loss_events still above 1 per run, sensing position is not the limit, and the next test should change controller.sensor_weights scaling, not gains or geometry size.
requested_changes: If s-bend finishes stay at 18/20 or better and slalom progress rises above 0.47 with fewer line-loss events, keep geometry.sensor_positions at y 0.07 and try y 0.08 (the allowed maximum) as the next single step, since iteration 6 showed the sensing layout is the cleaner lever than gain.

If s-bend finishes drop below 18/20 or s-bend max_error rises above about 0.02, return geometry.sensor_positions y to 0.06 with all other iteration-6 values, because iteration 8 showed the wider or larger footprint hurt s-bend and the forward shift may add the same kind of lag.

If slalom progress stays near 0.47 with line_loss_events still above 1 per run at y 0.07, leave the gains and geometry size alone and test controller.sensor_weights with a smaller outer-weight magnitude (for example [-1.5, -1.0, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5]), keeping the sign convention, to check whether the signal saturates at the outer sensors on tight bends.
